thread:
maya: Heads-up — p95 spike on /generate-route after the kernel selector tweak. p95 170ms -> 420ms on medium-length convos. Saw this right after the canary roll.
cheng: Any flamegraphs or quick profiles? which kernel path bubbled up?
maya: Quick log sample: `kernel=fast_attn_v2 seq=512 batch=8 kv_hits=0.2` — KV cache hit rate dropped, microbatch windows stretched, queue stacked.
raul: I profiled one replica. Softmax slow-path gets hot when batch sizes oscillate. Also saw the new 'queue-turnstile' metric spike — early cutoff is leaving lots of partial microbatches.
perf-bot: ALERT: route=generate p95 > SLO (5m avg).
cheng: Hypothesis: dynamic token-budget targets by route/tier are too aggressive for long-prefix routes — they get starved. Propose experiment: set `turnstile_threshold=0.3` and widen per-route KV-preserve window.
maya: Pushing a canary: `turnstile_threshold=0.35` + conservative kernel fallback for seq>256. Deploying now.
raul: Also capture `queue_wait_histogram` and `kv_cache_eviction_rate` for the next 30m.
maya: :thumbsup: + will snapshot `kernel_switch_count` too. If stable, fold into SLO-driven budgeter with per-route weights.
cheng: Note: when kernel switch happens mid-request we lose compiled kernel locality and add ~40ms jitter. Maybe add `kernel-stickiness` so we avoid switching until the microbatch completes.
maya: Good call — adding `kernel-stickiness=true` to the canary.
perf-bot: Canary deploy succeeded (2 nodes). Monitoring metrics now.
maya: Quick read after 15m: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 210ms on canary; kv_hit_rate up .2 -> .6. Will run A/B for 2h and collect traces.
raul: Also plan a synthetic stress job that mimics long conversation prefixes to validate token-budget fairness across tiers.
cheng: Follow-up: update eng-runtime dashboards to include `turnstile_ratio` and `kernel_switch_latency` so we can correlate regressions.
maya: Will add the dashboard and docs. Roll plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% if A/B holds for 2h and kv_evictions remain low.
raul: If the A/B shows any perf regressions, we should revert `fast_attn_v2` kernel selection for affected routes and iterate on batching window heuristics.
maya: Agreed. I'll post the perf traces and config diffs in the incident thread if anything regresses.
cheng: Thanks all — nice triage.
